notes.definition: Photosynthesis is the endothermic reaction in which plants and algae use energy transferred by light to make glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water. It takes place in the chloroplasts.
explanation: Photosynthesis is the process that green plants and algae use to make their own food. It happens inside chloroplasts, which contain a green pigment called chlorophyll. Chlorophyll absorbs light, and the energy transferred by the light is used to turn two simple, low-energy substances (carbon dioxide and water) into glucose, a sugar that stores energy in its chemical bonds. Oxygen is made as a by-product.

The word equation is: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, with light written above the arrow. You need to recognise the chemical symbols for each substance: carbon dioxide is CO₂, water is H₂O, glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆ and oxygen is O₂. The balanced symbol equation is 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂, but AQA only expects you to recognise the symbols.

Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction. This means energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light. The products (glucose and oxygen) have more energy stored in them than the reactants (carbon dioxide and water). This is the opposite of respiration, which is exothermic and transfers energy to the surroundings.

A land plant gets its raw materials from two places. Carbon dioxide diffuses from the air into the leaf through tiny pores called stomata, mostly on the underside of the leaf. Water is absorbed from the soil by root hair cells and travels up the stem to the leaves in the xylem. Most photosynthesis happens in the palisade mesophyll cells near the top of the leaf, because they are packed with chloroplasts and receive the most light.

Some of the oxygen made is used by the plant's own cells for respiration, and the rest diffuses out of the leaf through the stomata. The glucose is used by the plant in several ways, for example in respiration or to make starch, cellulose and proteins. Photosynthesis is vital for almost all life on Earth because it produces the oxygen we breathe and the glucose that forms the start of nearly every food chain.
keyFacts: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts of plant and algal cells.
Word equation: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (light energy needed).
Chemical symbols: CO₂ (carbon dioxide), H₂O (water), C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose), O₂ (oxygen).
Photosynthesis is endothermic: energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light.
Chlorophyll is the green pigment in chloroplasts that absorbs light.
Carbon dioxide enters the leaf by diffusion through the stomata.
Water is absorbed by root hair cells and carried to the leaves in the xylem.
Oxygen is a by-product and diffuses out of the leaf through the stomata.
Plants also respire all the time, day and night, but they only photosynthesise when there is light.

keyTerms.definition: The process in which plants and algae use energy transferred by light to make glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water.
A reaction that takes in energy from the surroundings, so the products store more energy than the reactants.
The organelle in plant and algal cells where photosynthesis takes place.
The green pigment inside chloroplasts that absorbs light energy.
Small pores, mainly on the underside of a leaf, that let carbon dioxide diffuse in and oxygen and water vapour diffuse out.
A simple sugar, C₆H₁₂O₆, made in photosynthesis; it stores energy in its chemical bonds.

equations.name: Photosynthesis (word equation)
equations.formula: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (light needed)
equations.units: no units (it is a chemical reaction)

workedExamples.title: Identifying reactants and products
workedExamples.question: A plant takes in CO₂ and H₂O and gives out O₂ in the light. Name the reactants and products of photosynthesis and give the symbol for the product that stays in the plant.
steps: Reactants are what goes into the reaction: carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O).
Products are what is made: glucose and oxygen (O₂).
Oxygen leaves through the stomata, so the product that stays in the plant is glucose.
The symbol for glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆.
workedExamples.answer: Reactants: carbon dioxide and water. Products: glucose and oxygen. Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) stays in the plant.

workedExamples.title: Explaining why photosynthesis is endothermic
workedExamples.question: Explain why photosynthesis is described as an endothermic reaction.
steps: Recall the definition: an endothermic reaction takes in energy from the surroundings.
Apply it: in photosynthesis, energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light.
Link to the products: this energy ends up stored in the chemical bonds of glucose, so the products store more energy than the reactants.
workedExamples.answer: Energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light and is stored in glucose, so the reaction takes in energy.

workedExamples.title: Where the raw materials come from
workedExamples.question: Describe how the raw materials for photosynthesis reach a palisade cell in a leaf.
steps: Carbon dioxide: it diffuses from the air into the leaf through the stomata, then through air spaces to the palisade cells.
Water: it is absorbed from the soil by root hair cells by osmosis.
The water is carried up the stem in the xylem to the leaf, then moves into the palisade cells.
workedExamples.answer: Carbon dioxide diffuses in through the stomata; water is absorbed by root hair cells and carried to the leaf in the xylem.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think plants get their food from the soil.
misconceptions.right: In fact plants make their own food (glucose) by photosynthesis from carbon dioxide and water. The soil supplies water and mineral ions, not food.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think plants photosynthesise instead of respiring.
misconceptions.right: In fact plants respire all the time, day and night. They only photosynthesise when there is light.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think photosynthesis gives out energy because it makes glucose, an energy store.
misconceptions.right: In fact photosynthesis is endothermic: it takes in energy transferred by light, and that energy becomes stored in glucose.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the oxygen plants make is used only by animals.
misconceptions.right: In fact plant cells use some of this oxygen for their own aerobic respiration; the rest diffuses out of the leaf.

realWorld: Almost all the oxygen in the atmosphere has been produced by photosynthesis in plants and algae, including huge amounts from algae in the oceans.
Crops such as wheat and rice get almost all of their mass from carbon dioxide taken from the air during photosynthesis, which is why farmers want plenty of light and carbon dioxide for their crops.
Forests and ocean algae remove large amounts of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, which helps to reduce the build-up of this greenhouse gas.
examTips: Learn the word equation exactly. A common error is writing 'water' as a product or 'oxygen' as a reactant.
When asked why photosynthesis is endothermic, say energy is transferred FROM the environment TO the chloroplasts by light. Just saying 'it needs light' is not enough.
Use the word 'diffuses' for carbon dioxide entering the leaf through the stomata, and 'xylem' for how water reaches the leaf.
Do not say light 'is turned into glucose'. Say energy transferred by light is stored in glucose.
summary: Photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts, where chlorophyll absorbs light.
Symbols: CO₂, H₂O, C₆H₁₂O₆ and O₂.
It is endothermic: energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light.
Carbon dioxide enters through stomata; water comes from the roots via the xylem.
Oxygen is a by-product; glucose is used by the plant.

markScheme: 1 mark: B (chloroplast)
questions.explanation: B is a chloroplast, which contains chlorophyll to absorb light for photosynthesis. A is a mitochondrion, where aerobic respiration happens. C is the nucleus, which holds the genetic material, and D is the permanent vacuole, which contains cell sap.

questions.question: Which gas is a reactant in photosynthesis?
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide and water are the reactants. Oxygen is a product, not a reactant. Nitrogen and hydrogen gas are not involved.

questions.question: Which pair of substances are both products of photosynthesis?
markScheme: 1 mark: glucose and oxygen
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis makes glucose and oxygen. Carbon dioxide and water are the reactants, which are used up. The other options mix a reactant with a product.

questions.question: Why is photosynthesis described as an endothermic reaction?
options: Energy is transferred to the surroundings during the reaction
Energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light
The reaction needs a high temperature to start
Oxygen is given out as a waste product
markScheme: 1 mark: energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light
questions.explanation: Endothermic reactions take in energy. In photosynthesis the energy comes from light. Transferring energy to the surroundings describes an exothermic reaction such as respiration. Giving out oxygen is true but does not explain why the reaction is endothermic.

questions.question: Which is the chemical formula for glucose?
markScheme: 1 mark: C₆H₁₂O₆
questions.explanation: Glucose has 6 carbon, 12 hydrogen and 6 oxygen atoms: C₆H₁₂O₆. CO₂ is carbon dioxide, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ is sucrose and C₆H₆O₆ has the wrong number of hydrogen atoms.

questions.question: Which substance in a leaf absorbs light for photosynthesis?
markScheme: 1 mark: chlorophyll
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in chloroplasts that absorbs light. Starch and cellulose are made from glucose, and glucose is a product of photosynthesis, not a light absorber.

questions.question: Where does most of the water used in photosynthesis by a land plant come from?
options: It is absorbed from the air through the stomata
It is made in the leaf by photosynthesis
It is carried down from the leaves in the phloem
It is absorbed from the soil by root hair cells and carried in the xylem
markScheme: 1 mark: absorbed from the soil by root hair cells and carried in the xylem
questions.explanation: Water enters root hair cells by osmosis and moves up the plant in the xylem. Water vapour actually leaves through the stomata. Phloem carries dissolved sugars, not the water used in photosynthesis.

questions.question: How does carbon dioxide enter a leaf?
options: By osmosis through the root hairs
By active transport through the waxy cuticle
Through the phloem from the roots
markScheme: 1 mark: by diffusion through the stomata
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a gas that diffuses from the air (higher concentration) into the leaf (lower concentration, because it is being used) through the stomata. Osmosis only describes water movement, and the waxy cuticle is waterproof and reduces gas exchange.

questions.question: A plant is sealed in a clear container and kept in bright light for several hours. What happens to the air in the container?
options: Carbon dioxide and oxygen concentrations both rise
Carbon dioxide rises and oxygen falls
Carbon dioxide falls and oxygen rises
Nothing changes because the plant does not use gases
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon dioxide falls and oxygen rises
questions.explanation: In bright light the plant photosynthesises faster than it respires, so it takes in more carbon dioxide and gives out more oxygen than respiration does the other way round. Carbon dioxide rising and oxygen falling would happen in the dark.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT needed for photosynthesis to take place?
markScheme: 1 mark: oxygen
questions.explanation: Oxygen is a product of photosynthesis, not something it needs. Light supplies the energy, chlorophyll absorbs the light and carbon dioxide is a reactant.

questions.question: Which organisms carry out photosynthesis?
markScheme: 1 mark: plants and algae
questions.explanation: Green plants and algae contain chloroplasts and photosynthesise. Fungi do not have chloroplasts and feed on other organisms. All living organisms respire, but not all photosynthesise.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the energy transfer in photosynthesis?
options: Energy transferred by light is stored as chemical energy in glucose
Energy stored in glucose is transferred to the surroundings as heat
Energy stored in carbon dioxide is transferred to oxygen
Energy from the soil is carried to the leaf by water
markScheme: 1 mark: energy transferred by light is stored as chemical energy in glucose
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light and the energy ends up in the chemical store of glucose. Releasing energy from glucose as heat describes respiration. The soil does not supply energy to the plant.

markScheme: 1 mark: C (palisade mesophyll)
questions.explanation: C is the palisade mesophyll. Its cells are near the top of the leaf where light is brightest and are packed with chloroplasts. A is the upper epidermis, which is mostly transparent with few chloroplasts. B is phloem and D is xylem, which are transport tissues.

questions.question:
A plant was kept in the dark for 2 days so its leaves contained no starch.
One leaf was then partly covered with foil, as shown in Figure 1. The plant was put in bright light for one day.
The leaf was then tested with iodine solution.
Which result and reason are correct for the covered part of the leaf?

figure.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 400 260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M40 130Q110 40 250 55Q330 80 370 130Q330 180 250 205Q110 220 40 130Z" fill="#86efac" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M40 130H370" stroke="currentColor"/><rect x="170" y="45" width="70" height="175" fill="#e5e7eb" fill-opacity="0.9" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="240" y1="100" x2="290" y2="20" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="150" y="15" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">foil covering both sides of leaf</text><line x1="100" y1="120" x2="80" y2="235" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="40" y="250" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">uncovered part of leaf</text></svg>

options: Turns blue-black, because starch is made all over the leaf
Stays orange-brown, because no light reached it so no glucose was made to turn into starch
Turns blue-black, because the covered part still contains chlorophyll
Stays orange-brown, because the foil killed the cells in that part
markScheme: 1 mark: stays orange-brown, because no light reached it so no glucose was made to turn into starch
questions.explanation: Without light there is no photosynthesis in the covered part, so no glucose is made and no starch is stored. Iodine stays orange-brown. Having chlorophyll is not enough: light is also needed. The foil does not kill the cells; it only blocks light.

questions.question:
Complete the word equation for photosynthesis.
........ + ........ → ........ + ........
markScheme: 1 mark: reactants carbon dioxide + water
1 mark: products glucose + oxygen
questions.explanation: The reactants (carbon dioxide and water) go on the left and the products (glucose and oxygen) on the right. Light can be written above the arrow because it supplies the energy, but it is not a reactant.

questions.question: Name the green pigment in chloroplasts that absorbs light.
markScheme: 1 mark: chlorophyll
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy. Do not confuse it with chloroplast, which is the organelle that contains chlorophyll.

questions.question: Give the chemical formulae of the two reactants in photosynthesis.
markScheme: 1 mark: CO₂ (carbon dioxide)
1 mark: H₂O (water)
questions.explanation: The reactants are carbon dioxide, CO₂, and water, H₂O. Watch the subscripts: CO is carbon monoxide, not carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Explain why photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction.
markScheme: 1 mark: energy is taken in / transferred from the environment (surroundings)
1 mark: to the chloroplasts by light / energy is stored in glucose
questions.explanation: An endothermic reaction takes in energy. In photosynthesis that energy is transferred by light from the environment to the chloroplasts, and is stored in the glucose made.

questions.question: Describe how a plant obtains the carbon dioxide and the water it needs for photosynthesis.
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon dioxide diffuses into the leaf through the stomata
1 mark: water is absorbed by root hair cells (by osmosis) and carried to the leaf in the xylem
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide comes from the air and diffuses in through stomata. Water comes from the soil, enters the root hair cells by osmosis and travels up the xylem.

questions.question: Give two reasons why photosynthesis is important for animals, including humans.
markScheme: 1 mark: it produces oxygen, which animals need for aerobic respiration
1 mark: it produces glucose / biomass, which is the source of food at the start of food chains
questions.explanation: Animals cannot make their own food. They rely on plants and algae for food (directly or through food chains) and for the oxygen they breathe.

questions.question: Give the chemical formula of the gas given off by a plant during photosynthesis.
markScheme: 1 mark: O₂
questions.explanation: Oxygen gas is O₂ because oxygen molecules are made of two oxygen atoms. 'O' on its own is a single atom and does not get the mark.

questions.question:
A student says, "A plant gets the food it needs to grow from the soil."
Explain why the student is wrong.
acceptedAnswers: soil provides water and mineral ions
markScheme: 1 mark: plants make their own food (glucose) by photosynthesis
1 mark: most of the mass comes from carbon dioxide taken in from the air (and water)
1 mark: the soil only supplies water and mineral ions, which are not food / not an energy source
questions.explanation: Glucose made in photosynthesis is the plant's food and is used to build new materials. Its carbon comes from carbon dioxide in the air. Mineral ions from the soil are needed in small amounts but do not provide energy.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows pondweed in bright light. Bubbles of gas are given off and collected.
Name the gas and describe a test to identify it.

markScheme: 1 mark: oxygen
1 mark: it relights a glowing splint
questions.explanation: The bubbles are mostly oxygen produced by photosynthesis. Oxygen relights a glowing splint. A lit splint with a squeaky pop is the test for hydrogen, which is a common confusion.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows a variegated leaf. The white area has no chlorophyll.
The leaf was kept in bright light for one day and then tested with iodine solution.
Only the green area turned blue-black.
Explain this result.

figure.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 400 262" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M40 130Q110 40 250 55Q330 80 370 130Q330 180 250 205Q110 220 40 130Z" fill="#e5e7eb" fill-opacity="0.3" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M75 130Q130 75 245 85Q310 100 335 130Q310 160 245 175Q130 185 75 130Z" fill="#86efac" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M40 130H370" stroke="currentColor"/><line x1="200" y1="110" x2="230" y2="20" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="200" y="15" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">green area (contains chlorophyll)</text><line x1="180" y1="207" x2="150" y2="245" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="60" y="255" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">white area (no chlorophyll)</text></svg>

markScheme: 1 mark: chlorophyll is needed to absorb light for photosynthesis
1 mark: so no photosynthesis / no glucose is made in the white areas
1 mark: in green areas glucose is made and converted to starch, which turns iodine blue-black
questions.explanation: This shows chlorophyll is needed for photosynthesis. Green areas make glucose and store some as starch, which iodine detects. White areas cannot absorb light, so they make no glucose and no starch.

markScheme: 1 mark: during the day, photosynthesis takes in carbon dioxide faster than respiration releases it
1 mark: at night there is no photosynthesis (no light) but respiration continues and releases carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Plants respire all the time. In daylight photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so there is a net uptake of carbon dioxide. In the dark only respiration happens, so carbon dioxide is released.

questions.question: Describe the process of photosynthesis in a leaf. In your answer, include where it happens, where the reactants come from and what the products are.
markScheme: Indicative content: happens in chloroplasts (in palisade cells); chlorophyll absorbs light; energy is transferred from the environment by light, so it is endothermic; carbon dioxide diffuses in through stomata; water absorbed by root hair cells and carried in the xylem; carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen; oxygen diffuses out through stomata (or is used in respiration); glucose used by the plant.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): a clear, linked description covering location, the sources of both reactants and both products, using correct terms such as stomata, xylem and chlorophyll.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct statements, such as naming reactants or products, but with little linking or with missing parts.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: A strong answer follows the journey: where light is absorbed, how each reactant arrives, the equation, and what happens to each product. Using key words like diffusion, stomata and xylem lifts the answer to Level 2.

questions.question:
In the 1600s a scientist planted a willow tree in a pot of dry soil. He gave the tree only rainwater for 5 years.
Table 1 shows his results.
He concluded that all of the tree's extra mass came from water.
Use your knowledge of photosynthesis to explain where the tree's extra mass came from, and evaluate the scientist's conclusion.

rows: Mass of dry soil in kg

markScheme: Indicative content: the soil lost only 0.06 kg, so very little mass came from the soil (only mineral ions); the tree gained 74.4 kg; the tree made glucose by photosynthesis from carbon dioxide and water; carbon dioxide was absorbed from the air through the stomata, which the scientist did not know about; glucose is used to make starch, cellulose, proteins and other substances, which form new biomass; so much of the mass (all of the carbon) came from carbon dioxide in the air; water did contribute (hydrogen and some oxygen in glucose), so the conclusion was partly correct; some water was also lost by evaporation and the mass measurements did not account for gases; the conclusion is therefore incomplete and only partly valid.

Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): a detailed and coherent explanation linking photosynthesis to the gain in mass, identifying carbon dioxide from the air as a major source, and a balanced evaluation stating the conclusion is partly correct (water contributes) but incomplete.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): a reasonable explanation that names photosynthesis and carbon dioxide as a source of mass, with some evaluation of the conclusion.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, for example that the soil did not provide the mass or that plants photosynthesise, with little linking.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that most of a plant's dry mass is built from carbon taken in as carbon dioxide during photosynthesis. Water is also a reactant, so the scientist was partly right, but he missed the role of the air. A top answer uses the data (74.4 kg gained, 0.06 kg lost from soil) and gives a judgement.

questions.question: At night a plant gives out carbon dioxide but no oxygen. Which statement explains this?
options: Photosynthesis stops without light, but respiration continues all the time
Stomata release carbon dioxide stored during the day
markScheme: 1 mark: photosynthesis stops without light, but respiration continues all the time
questions.explanation: Respiration happens day and night in every living cell and releases carbon dioxide. Photosynthesis needs light, so at night no oxygen is produced. Plants do not respire only at night, and chlorophyll does not break down each night.
